resources.string: Set up the Volume, Mute, Power and Input buttons of your remote so they control your TV, or make the remote beep when it is lost.
The TV buttons were last set up for: %1$s.
a TV whose brand is not listed
This device has Google\'s own remote setup, under Settings, Remotes and accessories. Use that one instead: the two would overwrite each other.
Send the saved setup to a remote
Remove the TV buttons from the remote
Volume, Mute, Power and Input will stop controlling the TV and act on this box again. You can set them up again at any time.
The remote\'s buttons act on this box again.

For a TV this app has no code for. Put a file named profile.json here:
%1$s

It lists a Pronto hex code for each button, for example:
{"volume_up": "0000 006D …", "volume_down": "…", "mute": "…", "power": "…", "input": "…"}
Send the file\'s codes to the remote
That file could not be used: %1$s

Version %1$s

Remotesmith sets up the TV buttons of remotes built on Google's reference design, the way the box they shipped with would. It is not affiliated with Google.

TV codes come from the IRext database (MIT licence, © 2019 IRext) and from Flipper-IRDB files given under CC0.

The app is free software under the Apache licence 2.0.
Sending the codes to the remote…
The setup is on the remote
Point the remote at the TV and try the buttons.
Press any button on the remote to wake it, then try again.\n\nIf it still does not answer, check its batteries.

No remote is paired with this box yet.

Open Settings, Remotes and accessories, Pair accessory. Then hold Back and Home on the remote until its light pulses.

A remote that was paired here before may need a reset first: hold Mute and the centre button until the light stays on.
Bluetooth is switched off on this box. Turn it on in Settings, then try again.
The app needs permission to use Bluetooth to talk to the remote.
This remote cannot do that. The app works with remotes built on Google\'s reference design, such as the Google TV Streamer and Chromecast voice remotes.
The remote stopped answering part-way. Keep it close and try again.

You pick your TV's brand, then try codes until the TV answers. It takes a few minutes.

Keep the remote pointed at the TV while you test.

This replaces any TV buttons the remote has now.
Point the remote at the TV. Press Volume Up a few times, then Volume Down, and hold one of them for a moment.\n\nDid the TV\'s volume follow?
Press Mute.\n\nDid the TV mute? Press it again to bring the sound back.

Read this first, because the screen will go dark:

1. Press Power. The TV should turn off.
2. Wait about 10 seconds.
3. Press Power again and wait for the picture.
Then answer below.
Press the ★ button (on some remotes it is marked Input).\n\nThe TV should show its list of inputs. If the picture switches away from this screen, keep pressing until it comes back.
It turned off and back on
It turned off but not back on
None of the %1$s codes moved the volume
Next come the most common codes from other brands. Many TVs answer to one of them.
No code moved the TV\'s volume
Check that nothing blocks the front of the remote and that its batteries are fresh, then try again.\n\nIf your TV really is not covered, you can add its codes yourself under More, Use my own codes.
That button is left without a TV code and keeps acting on this box.
The TV did not come back on
Turn the TV on with its own button or its own remote.\n\nSome TVs ignore Power for a few seconds after turning off. If this happens again, skip Power.
The buttons you confirmed so far stay on the remote. The rest keep acting on this box.
Nothing was confirmed yet, so the remote goes back to how it was set up before.
Working with the TV now: %1$s.\n\nThe codes are stored in the remote itself, so they keep working, even with another box. A copy is kept here in case you want to send it to a second remote.
The remote beeps for up to 30 seconds. Press any button on it to stop the sound.
The remote is asleep. It will beep as soon as it wakes up, which can take a few minutes. Keep this screen open.
Found: a button was pressed on the remote.
The remote\'s batteries are too low to beep.
